messages:
sam: Opening thread: bundling strategy followup. we need to decide shadow-eval vs hot-swap semantics and how to load big bundles without OOMing nodes. quick bullets.
dina: shadow-eval meaning we keep old bundle active and run new bundle in parallel for a subset of requests to compare outputs?
sam: yes. idea: route 0.5% of traffic to new bundle in shadow mode (no side effects) and record decisions for sim. once metrics look good, flip pointer.
omar: +1 but shadow mode doubles memory if both bundles fully materialize. any options to reduce overhead?
tess: we can memory-map bundles and rely on OS page sharing if bundles share string tables / interned ids. big win if we compact during bundling.
sam: good point. proposal: bundler emits: 1) compacted bundle blob (content-addressed), 2) a small in-memory index for fast lookup. runtime mmaps blob, builds tiny in-memory index (~1-2MB) and points to offsets.
dina: tradeoff: mmapped blobs are fast but harder to iterate in-process for simulation. sims want a materialized API. maybe simulator loads a light-weight interpreter that reads mmapped structures lazily.
omar: another option: sub-bundles split by tenant-affinity or route prefix. can lazy-load sub-bundle on first access. that reduces peak mem for shadowing most of the time.
ops-automation: ops ask: how do we GC old bundles? cant keep infinite mmaps. need TTL + refcount.
sam: GC plan: bundle refcount tracked per-process (atomic pointer + per-tenant usage counters). central catalog keeps last-used timestamp. GC job deletes content blobs after N days if no refs.
tess: safety: what about partial failure during flip? we should support two-phase flip: write new bundle -> update catalog -> per-process reload signal -> once 100% ack, mark old bundle deprecated. rollback path: set catalog pointer back.
dina: latency tradeoffs: mmapped loads are cheap but first access to a sub-bundle causes page fault and stalls. we should prefetch hot sub-bundles during canary ramp.
omar: we also need determinism for tests: mmapped layout must be canonical, bundle creation should be content-addressed so validator can compare bitwise.
runtime-bot: quick perf note: simulated mmapped load with 5k routes shows first-touch spike ~50ms on 95p, subsequent steady-state negligible. shadowing with separate mmaps increased RSS by ~12% in our test cluster.
sam: thread decision candidates: A) use mmapped content-addressed bundles + small index + lazy sub-bundle loads + shadowing via per-tenant pointer to new bundle. B) keep in-memory materialized bundles only, more memory but simpler semantics. my vote: A.
dina: vote A but need strong bundler compaction and canonicalization. also we need a compatibility layer for older runtimes that expect materialized structures.
omar: add opt-in flag for runtime: --enable-mmap-bundles to allow ramp. ops-automation: also add upload-size limit (e.g., 25MB) and automatic sub-bundle suggestion if over limit.
ops-automation: suggest API changes: POST /policy-bundles returns {bundle_id, size_bytes, compacted_hash, sub_bundles:[ids], manifest_sig}. Add GET /policy-bundles/:id/preview which returns index summary (no heavy payload).
sam: observability: record bundle_id on request trace and emit metrics: bundle.load_time_ms, subbundle_prefetch_ms, pagefault_spike_count.
tess: one more: live debug hook. /debug/bundles?show=heap lets us inspect which sub-bundles are mmapped and their refcounts. limit this to internal-only.
dina: open question: how to validate sub-bundle cross-references? we must ensure references from route->scorer exist across sub-bundles or bundler must inline dependency graph to avoid runtime misses.
sam: bundler will emit a dependency index and validator will fail bundles where unresolved refs exist unless the bundle explicitly declares cross-load policies. we'll add lint rule: no unresolved references in default tenancy scope.
runtime-bot: queued: larger sim for multi-tenant cold-starts. will report results under #architecture this afternoon.
omar: volunteers to own rollout runbook? I can draft it. include precheck script that runs validator + dry-run mmapped load on a staging fleet.
sam: perfect. I'll add these notes to the RFC addendum and propose a week timeline for a canary. thanks all.
